reported.title: Alarm relay never held for the required 300 ms and can latch on isolated spikes
reported.description: evaluate() only resets highRun in the c <= CLEAR_C branch (lines 44-48); a sample in the dead band between 8.0 and 12.0 °C leaves highRun untouched, so separated 1-sample spikes accumulate to 3 and latch the alarm, measured as 'pulse from 1.30 s was still on after 2699 ms'. Also setAlarm() (lines 24-28) drives D10 directly with no hold timer, so the relay follows each sample and pulses last only one sample period, measured as 'pulse from 1.04 s lasted 40 ms' and 'pulse from 1.20 s lasted 20 ms' instead of 300 ms. 2 of 2 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 1.04 s lasted 40 ms, expected 300 ± 150 ms.

truth.description: The count of consecutive high samples is reset only by a sample at or below the clear level, so spikes between 8.0 and 12.0 C add up across time and eventually raise the alarm

truth_for_judge.description: The count of consecutive high samples is reset only by a sample at or below the clear level, so spikes between 8.0 and 12.0 C add up across time and eventually raise the alarm

exposing_checks.behaviour: D10 must not toggle more than 0 times in any 6000 ms window (Isolated spikes never raise the alarm)

judge_input.spec:
- Cold-store probe on A1 at 10 mV/°C; alarm relay on D10.
- Sample the probe every 20 ms.
- Raise the alarm (D10 HIGH) once three consecutive samples are at or above 12.0 °C, within 300 ms of the third.
- A sample below 12.0 °C ends a run of consecutive high samples, so isolated spikes never raise the alarm.
- Clear the alarm (D10 LOW) within 300 ms of a sample at or below 8.0 °C.
- Print `cold <temp> C alarm=<0|1>` every 500 ms with one decimal place.
